questions.q: Write a PETZAAL Point, Evidence and Zoom in: 'How does Shakespeare present Prospero's power?'
questions.a: For example: Prospero is presented as all-powerful: he raised the storm, yet he promises 'not so much perdition as an hair' was lost; 'hair' shows his total control.

questions.q: How does Prospero treat Miranda and Ariel differently? One sentence each.
questions.a: Miranda: gentle and protective, he explains their past. Ariel: commanding, he praises but also threatens.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PETZAAL paragraph: 'How does Shakespeare present Prospero in Act 1 scene 2?' Starter: 'Shakespeare presents Prospero as...'
questions.a: A PETZAAL paragraph on power, control or care, with a short embedded quotation and an Alternative.

questions.q: Extend: is Prospero a victim or a tyrant? Choose and justify.
questions.a: Both: he was wronged by Antonio, but he controls Ariel and Caliban harshly.

questions.q: Stretch: why might Shakespeare give such a long exposition in scene 2?
questions.a: The audience needs the backstory to understand the revenge plot; the storm made them curious first.

questions.q: Why is the audience calm while the courtiers panic?
options: We know Prospero's magic means no one has died
We know the ship will sink
questions.a: A) We know Prospero's magic means no one has died. This is dramatic irony; B is wrong (the ship is safe); C ignores the drama.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: was Prospero's love of study a fault?
questions.a: Partly: he neglected his duty as ruler, which gave Antonio the chance to take power.
